title: The Weight of an Elephant
summary: Akbar is challenged to weigh a massive war elephant without a scale. Birbal uses water displacement and riverboats to solve the riddle.
full_text:
The King of Persia sent Emperor Akbar a colossal royal gift: a magnificent, battle-hardened war elephant named Airavat, towering twelve cubits high, with tusks wrapped in gold bands. Along with the beast came a playful diplomatic challenge:

'Greetings to Emperor Akbar. We gift you this majestic beast, but challenge your renowned scholars to determine its exact weight down to the last ser. However, no scale in Hindustan is large enough to hold an elephant, nor may the animal be harmed or starved!'

Akbar assembled the master engineers, blacksmiths, and mathematicians of Agra. Some proposed building a colossal balance beam using thirty iron chains and giant stone counterweights, but the cost would bankrupt the treasury, and no tree was strong enough to support the fulcrum. Others proposed weighing the elephant's food and droppings, which drew only laughter. The court was at a standstill.

Akbar turned to Birbal: 'Can an elephant be weighed without a giant scale?'

'Easily, Your Majesty,' Birbal replied. 'All we need is a large cargo barge on the river Yamuna, a box of red chalk, and a bag of stones.'

The court marched to the riverbank. Birbal had a massive, flat-bottomed cargo boat tied securely to the wooden pier.

First, Birbal led the heavy war elephant across a ramp onto the boat. Under the immense weight of the beast, the barge sank deep into the river water.

Birbal took a piece of red chalk, knelt at the water's edge, and drew a clear, straight horizontal line all along the hull of the boat, exactly at the water level.

Next, Birbal led the elephant back off the boat onto dry land. With the weight removed, the empty barge rose high in the water, the red chalk line now floating well above the surface.

Birbal then ordered royal laborers to fill the boat with heavy river stones from the shore, shoveling stone after stone into the hold until the boat sank once again—down, down, down—until the water level touched the red chalk line with exact precision!

'Now,' Birbal smiled at Emperor Akbar, 'remove the stones from the boat in ordinary sacks and weigh them on our standard marketplace scales! The total weight of the stones will equal the exact weight of the elephant!'

The Persian ambassador gasped in awe. The solution was so breathtakingly simple, so scientifically elegant, that the entire assembly erupted in thunderous acclaim. Akbar rewarded Birbal with a golden robe, remarking that true intellect finds solutions in the simplest laws of nature.
